relations.subject: js-udf:udf-library
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (usesEnum) - global/scoped is a closed two-value choice for a library's access level, same shape as other enum relations in the registry
relations.evidence: A JavaScript library can be **global** or **scoped**. * A **global** library is created within the `default:` namespace, at the same level as the buckets in your database. A global library is available to all clients.

relations.subject: js-udf:udf-library
relations.evidence: * A **scoped** library is created within a scope, at the same level as the collections within the scope. A scoped library is only available to clients that have access to that bucket and scope. Use a scoped JavaScript library to keep the code for user-defined functions separate.

relations.subject: js-udf:udf-library
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - deleting a library is gated on first dropping all functions that reference it
relations.evidence: Before you can delete a library, you must first drop all SQL++ user-defined functions which point to any of the JavaScript functions within that library. For more information, see [DROP FUNCTION](../n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/dropfunction.md).

relations.subject: js-udf:udf-library
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - structural procedure, describes the UI path exclusively (no SQL++ CREATE FUNCTION equivalent is shown on this page for creating a library itself)
relations.evidence: 1. On the **Operational Clusters** page, select the operational cluster where you want to work with user-defined functions. 2. Go to **Data Tools** → **Query**. 3. In the Data Insights area, to the left of the query editor, find the **Functions** section. 4. Next to the **Functions** section header, go to **Create (+)** → **Library**.
